names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Αντώνιος, Ιωάννης οι αυτάδελφοι και Ευστάθιος οι Μάρτυρες», with the rank words left off; the life page heads him «Αγιος Ιωάννης (; - 1347)».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 14 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. муч. Антоније, Јован и Евстатије.“, where Св. муч. heads the three and belongs to no one of them, so each forename stands bare. The heading gives no epithet and does not name Vilnius, which is in the body and which this corpus keeps in the display name. The bare form is shared with five other folders and that fold is deliberate and recorded. This is also the folder's second name form of any kind: it held only the Greek Ιωάννης.

death.note: saint.gr: «μαζί με τον Ευστάθιο μαρτύρησαν το έτος 1347 στη Βίλνα της Λιθουανίας», and the page heads each of the three «(; - 1347)»; no year of birth is printed.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Αντώνιος, Ιωάννης οι αυτάδελφοι και Ευστάθιος οι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The whole body of the page is two sentences: «Οι Άγιοι Μάρτυρες Αντώνιος και Ιωάννης ήταν αδέλφια και μαζί με τον Ευστάθιο μαρτύρησαν το έτος 1347 στη Βίλνα της Λιθουανίας. Τα ιερά λείψανα αυτών φυλάσσονται στην ιερά μονή Αγίας Τριάδος Βίλνας.» Under «Ιερά Λείψανα» it adds a line for each of the three separately, putting his relics in the church of the Holy Spirit at Vilnius in Lithuania — so the page names two resting places and does not reconcile them. It gives no parentage, no trade, no account of the trial, no judge and no hymn, and no couplet. The corpus holds no other saint of Vilna; the many folders named Anthony, John and Eustathius are other men on other days.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 27.04.2026 (14. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Антоније, Јован и Евстатије.“

attestations.note: Second of the three the day's second heading enumerates, on the same menologion day the Greek keeps all three on; the Russian and Romanian rows stay `undocumented`. The **1347 agrees exactly** with what this folder holds, so **no date was touched**. New: the three as **pagans and worshippers of fire** and **servants at the court of the Lithuanian prince Olgard at Vilnius**; the three pagan names **Kruglec, Kumec and Nezhilo**, given as a set and **not assigned to any one of them**, the entry listing them in one clause without saying whose was whose; the **baptism by a priest the entry names Нестор**; the **hanging of all three, one after another, on one and the same oak**; and the **oak cut down by the Christians, the church of the Holy Trinity built, the relics laid in it and the holy table made out of the stump**, the relics being at Vilnius. **The fold on the stored form is deliberate and it is the widest this wave has met**: a bare Јован is held by five other folders — `john-of-edessa`, `john-of-konitsa`, `john-of-novgorod`, `john-of-sfakia-new-martyr` and `john-son-of-xenophon` — and this heading, which puts Св. муч. over three names, gives no epithet and no city. Recorded in the run's findings. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
